gap: No result ChatGPT got works out the cost of adding NAS runtime while keeping the USB shutdown link. EcoFlow's DELTA 3 Series Smart Extra Battery adds 1,024 Wh for $388 ($0.38/Wh). The RIVER 3 Plus EB300 adds 286 Wh for $149 ($0.52/Wh), and the RIVER 3 Plus stops at 858 Wh. Measured DELTA 3 Plus output is 910 Wh per 1,024 Wh, so DELTA 3 Plus plus one extra battery gives about 57 h on a 32 W 2-bay NAS and about 31 h on a 59 W 4-bay NAS.
standout_why: I compared against computingforgeeks.com/power-station-vs-ups-homelab. It has runtimes using 73% of nameplate, plus prices for the River 3 Plus (about $299), C1000 Gen 2, AC180 and others. It has no extra-battery pricing, no DELTA 3 Plus or DELTA 3 Ultra runtime, and no cost per usable Wh. racksandwatts.com uses a 15 W overhead formula but lists no prices and only covers the RIVER 3 Max and AC180. thepowerstationguide.com/blog/portable-power-station-vs-ups (cited) gives only UPS minute runtimes and a vague 'many hours' for 288 Wh, with no prices. None of them work out the cost of runtime for the models that have a data port, or cover the DELTA 3 Ultra / Ultra Plus, whose USB-C UPS-HID support EcoFlow documents.
decides: The USB shutdown requirement leaves only EcoFlow units with a data port: RIVER 3 Plus (USB-B), DELTA 3 Plus (USB-C) and DELTA 3 Ultra / Ultra Plus (USB-C UPS-HID). Among those, the pick depends on how many NAS hours you need. Up to a few hours: RIVER 3 Plus. Overnight or more: DELTA 3 Plus, adding the $388 extra battery if needed. That costs less per added Wh than stacking RIVER 3 Plus EB300s, and the RIVER 3 Plus tops out at 858 Wh. If you need 2 days or more on a 4-bay NAS, the DELTA 3 Ultra at $1,299 for 3,072 Wh ($0.42/Wh nominal) has the lowest cost per hour of any unit with a data port. This supports ChatGPT's RIVER 3 Plus / DELTA 3 Plus split and adds a price-based reason to choose the Ultra.
